content.title: About
content.content: Anchovies are small marine fish of the Engraulidae family, found in the warm waters of the Atlantic, Mediterranean and Black Seas. They are commonly sold salted, marinated or canned and add a strong, savory flavor to many dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Anchovies are often called “sea salt” because their intense taste enhances the flavor of other ingredients.
They are a staple in Italian cuisine (pizza, puttanesca sauce) and Spanish tapas (anchovy sauce, escarola).
Two main species are used: European anchovy (Engraulis encrasicolus) and California anchovy (Engraulis mordax).
Canned anchovies are usually packed in oil or brine, preserving their softness and aroma.
Anchovies are rich in omega‑3 fatty acids, beneficial for heart health.

items.title: Rich in omega‑3
items.content: Omega‑3 fatty acids help maintain healthy cholesterol levels and reduce inflammation.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: About 20 g of complete protein per 100 g, supporting muscle and tissue maintenance.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Contains B12, niacin and riboflavin, which are important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Mineral source
items.content: Provides calcium, iron, magnesium and selenium, essential for bones, blood and antioxidant defense.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: Despite their strong flavor, anchovies are relatively low‑calorie when eaten without excess oil.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: People allergic to seafood may experience reactions ranging from mild to anaphylactic.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Salted and canned anchovies contain a lot of salt, which can be problematic for hypertension or kidney issues.

items.title: Heavy‑metal contamination risk
items.content: Like other marine fish, anchovies can accumulate mercury and other toxins; choose reputable sources.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Anchovies are commonly added to sauces, salads, pastas and pizza. Use them as a flavor enhancer, mash into a paste, or serve whole as a snack. Pairing with oil or lemon brightens their taste.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store unopened canned anchovies in a cool, dry place. After opening, transfer to an airtight container and keep refrigerated for 3–5 days. Dried salted anchovies should be kept in the fridge to prevent spoilage.
